title: Bright Field Standard Swarming Imaging
author: Serena Ding
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.vybe7sn
materials: Images are segmented in real time by the Gecko software.

steps.title: Prepare imaging plates
steps.instruction: Pour 3.5 mL low‑peptone (0.013 % Difco Bacto) NGM agar (2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene) into 35 mm Petri dishes exactly seven days before each imaging day, store the plates at 4 °C, then dry them agar‑side down at 37 °C overnight.

steps.title: Seed bacteria lawn
steps.instruction: One to three hours before imaging, place a single 20 µL spot of cold diluted OP50 (OD = 0.75) at the center of each dried imaging plate to create a uniform lawn and avoid the coffee‑ring effect.

steps.title: Synchronize worms by bleach
steps.instruction: Bleach‑synchronize gravid hermaphrodites and keep the synchronized worms on a rotator at 20 °C until they are needed for the experiment.

steps.title: Re‑feed starved L1 worms
steps.instruction: Using a glass pipette, transfer starved L1 worms onto three to four culture plates (55 mm Petri dishes containing 15 mL low‑peptone 0.013 % Difco Bacto NGM agar, 2 % Bio/Agar, BioGene) that have been seeded with OP50, then incubate the plates at 20 °C.

steps.title: Transfer worms to imaging plate
steps.instruction: With a glass pipette, move exactly forty worms onto the imaging plate in a small drop of M9 buffer, placing the drop away from the bacterial lawn.

steps.title: Acquire swarming recordings
steps.instruction: Immediately after transfer, record the worms on a custom six‑camera rig (Phoenix) equipped with Dalsa Genie cameras (G2‑GM10‑T2041) using red 630 nm LED illumination (CCS Inc.) for seven hours at 25 Hz with Gecko software (v2.0.3.1), while maintaining the plate at 20 °C throughout the acquisition.

steps.title: Wash worms from culture plates
steps.instruction: Wash the worms off the culture plates with M9 buffer, collect the suspension in a 15 mL Falcon tube, perform two additional washes with M9, and aspirate as much supernatant as possible after the final wash.

steps.title: Trim recordings post‑acquisition
steps.instruction: Manually truncate each recording to retain only the aggregation and swarming phases: define the start time as when the liquid drop dries and all worms exit the initial location, and the end time as when food is depleted and worms disperse with increased crawling speed.
